summary.text: … is a type of Japanese multi-coloured woodblock printing; the technique is used primarily in ukiyo-e. It was invented in the 1760s, and perfected and popularized by the printmaker Suzuki Harunobu, who produced many nishiki-e prints between 1765 and his death five years later.
A nishiki-e print is created by carving a separate woodblock for every colour, and using them in a stepwise fashion.
